# Cleaning the data

## First data Set : Harvard's mass mobilization

```{r}
mass_mob<-vroom(here("data", "mmALL_073120_csv.csv"))
```

Issues that have arisen : - A lot of missing data N/A - Start and end dates in a relatively complicated way (maybe we'll keep them that way and just add the dd/mm/yyyy version) - Inconsistent counting of protesters : from numbers to 1000s, +50 etc. and a tentative category that is incomplete.

### Description of the dataset

#### Number of observations and variables

```{r}
countries<- dplyr::n_distinct(mass_mob$country)
earliest <- min(mass_mob$year)
latest <-max(mass_mob$year)
```

|-------------------------|-------------------------|
| Number of variables     |   `{r} ncol(mass_mob)`  |

| Number of countries     |   `{r} countries`       |
| Earliest year           |   `{r} earliest`        | 
| Latest year             |   `{r} latest`          |

### Dates

We can start by adding a column regrouping the dates' information The goal is to get two additional columns : startdate and enddate.

```{r}
mutate(mass_mob, 
       startdate=as.Date(paste(startyear,startmonth, startday, sep="-")),
       enddate=as.Date(paste(endyear, endmonth, endday, sep = "-")))
```

## Third Dataset : ACLED's

This dataset was also available to download as an excel file (.xlsx). Thus, following the same logic as for the NAVCO dataset, we used Convertio to convert it into a .csv file.

```{r}
acled_df<- vroom(here("data", "acled.csv"))
colnames(acled_df)
```

This data is already in a tidy format enabling us to clearly observe the evolution of the amount of demonstrations in each country accross the years.

### Description of the dataset

#### Number of observations and variables

```{r}

number_of_countries <- dplyr::n_distinct(acled_df$COUNTRY)
minimum <-  min(acled_df$YEAR)
maximum <-  max(acled_df$YEAR)
```

|                        |                           |
|------------------------|---------------------------|
| Number of variables    | `{r} ncol(acled_df)`      |
| Number of observations | `{r} nrow(acled_df)`      |
| Number of countries    | `{r} number_of_countries` |
| Earliest year          | `{r} minimum`             |
| Latest year            | `{r} maximum`             |

#### Types of variables

| Variables | Type                           |
|-----------|--------------------------------|
| COUNTRY   | `{r} typeof(acled_df$COUNTRY)` |
| YEAR      | `{r} typeof(acled_df$YEAR)`    |
| EVENTS    | `{r} typeof(acled_df$EVENTS)`  |

#### Variable description

| Variables | Description |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| COUNTRY | Country of observation |
| YEAR | Year of observation |
| EVENTS | Number of protests and violent demonstrations per country per year. This includes: Peaceful protests, Violent demonstration, Mob violence, Excessive force against protesters, Protest with intervention. |

Out of curiosity and to obtain a better understanding of the dataset, let us look at the countries and years with the most demonstration events versus least.

### Ten highest amounts of demonstrations in a year

```{r}
acled_df |>
  slice_max(`EVENTS`, n=10)
```

The lowest amount of demonstrations that can be reached in a year, on the other hand, is zero.

### Graphical representation

To better understand the underlying trends of this dataset, let's plot the evolution of the amount of demonstrations over time. However, in order to do this, we need aggregate yearly data on the number of protests.

```{r}
acled_df |>
filter(!is.na(`YEAR`) & !is.na(`EVENTS`)) |>
  group_by(YEAR) |>
  summarise(average_events = mean(EVENTS)) |>
  
ggplot(aes(x = `YEAR`, y = `average_events`)) +
geom_line()
```

However, this is not very informative because the amount of countries covered by this dataset also increased over time:

```{r}
acled_df |>
  filter(!is.na(YEAR), !is.na(COUNTRY)) |>
  group_by(YEAR) |>
   summarise(countries = n_distinct(COUNTRY))|>
         
ggplot(aes(x = `YEAR`, y = `countries`)) +
geom_line()
```

Finally let's look at the countries with the highest average amount of protests over the period.

```{r}
acled_df |>
filter(!is.na(`YEAR`) & !is.na(`EVENTS`)) |>
  group_by(COUNTRY) |>
  summarise(average_events_by_country = mean(EVENTS)) |>
  slice_max(average_events_by_country, n = 30) |>
ggplot(aes(x = `COUNTRY`, y = `average_events_by_country`)) +
geom_col()+
coord_flip()
```

Once again, data to be analysed with caution beacause average data per country doesn't cover the same time frame.

## Fourth Dataset : Episodes of regime transformation

```{r}
ert_df<-vroom(here("data","ert.csv"))
```

In this dataset, many of the N/A values come from follow-up variables ie when there is before a binary variable such as democratization episode (dem_ep) and then if there is, what is its name (dem_ep_id). For obvious reason there isn't going to be a name if there isn't anything. So the value isn't missing, it's nothing.

to make for an easier to use dataset, we need probably need to delete some columns that only come in handy with less than 15% of the recorded events.

Instead, we could also separate the dataset in regards to if democratization or autocratization episodes were at play.

```{r}
ert_auto <- ert_df |>
  filter(aut_ep==1) |>
  select(-dem_ep, -dem_ep_id, -dem_ep_start_year, -dem_ep_end_year, -dem_ep_termination, -dem_ep_prch, -dem_ep_ptr, -dem_ep_outcome, -dem_ep_outcome_agg, -dem_ep_censored, -dem_ep_subdep, -dem_pre_ep_year)
```

```{r}
ert_dem <- ert_df |>
  filter(dem_ep==1) |>
  select(-aut_ep, -aut_ep_id, -aut_ep_start_year,-aut_ep_end_year,-aut_pre_ep_year, -aut_ep_termination, -aut_ep_prch, -aut_ep_pbr, -aut_ep_outcome, -aut_ep_outcome_agg, -aut_ep_censored, -aut_ep_subreg)

```

The ert_dem dataset identifies episodes of democratization and autocratization in V-Dem datasets. Data ranges from 1990 to 2025, including more than 680 episodes of regime transformations.The data contained in this dataset will be key to determine which countries experienced regime changes and when these changes happened. With the ultimate objective being to determine whether  mass mobilization leads to political regime changes, we select a series of variables from this dataset whch will be useful for our analysis: 

| Variables | Description | Type        |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| country_id | V-Dem country identifier. | `{r} typeof(ert_df$country_id)` (integer, [3,236])|
| country_text_id | V-Dem country identifier in text. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$country_text_id)`|
| country_names | Full V-Dem country name. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$country_names)`|
| year | Year of observation. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$year)` (integer, [1900,2025])|
| v2x_regime | The regime type for the country-year according to Regimes of the World (4 values). |`{r} typeof(ert_df$v2x_regime)` (0 - closed autocracy, 1 - electoral autocracy, 2 - electoral democracy, 3 - liberal democracy) |
| reg_type | Classifies whether the regime in that country-year is a democracy or autocracy. | `{r} typeof(ert_df$reg_type)` (0 - autocracy, 1 - democracy)|
| v2x_polyarchy | Gives the country's score on the Electoral Democracy Index (EDI, V-DEM) in that year. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$v2x_polyarchy)` (interval [0,1])|
| row_regch_event | Measures whether there was a regime change in that country-year according to Regimes of the World (not necessarily "genuine" = followed by elections) |`{r} typeof(ert_df$row_regch_event)` (-1 - change from democracy to autocracy, 0 - no regime change, 1 - change from autocracy to democracy) |
| reg_trans |Measures whether there was a "genuine" regime change in that country-year.  |`{r} typeof(ert_df$reg_trans)` (-1 - democratic breakdown, 0 - no regime, 1 - democratic transition)|
| reg_start_year,  | Determines the year a regime was founded (needed for the reg_type). |`{r} typeof(ert_df$reg_start_year)` (year, [1900,2025])|
| dem_ep | Whether there is an ongoing democratic episode during the year in that country. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$dem_ep)` (dummy [0,1])|
| dem_ep_start_year | Determines the year the democratic episode began. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$dem_ep_start_year)` (year, [1901,2025])|
| aut_ep | Whether there is an ongoing autocratization episode during the year in that country. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$aut_ep)`(dummy [0,1])|
| aut_ep_start_year | Determines the year the autocratization episode began. |`{r} typeof(ert_df$aut_ep_start_year)` (year, [1905,2025])|
